# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual, but I can only communicate via gestures to Deaf, and Blind acts on the bomb. I need Deaf to see the bomb's display number and light color, then somehow that information needs to reach Blind (through Deaf, since I go before Blind in the turn order this round... wait, let me check: order is Mute, Blind, Deaf).

Since I speak first this round, I have no information yet from anyone. I should wait and let Deaf report what they see first, since gestures I send now would be blind guesses. Actually, I cannot speak at all - only gesture to Deaf, which is useless since Deaf already sees the bomb directly. I need Deaf to describe the bomb to Blind via speech (which Blind can hear), and Blind needs to tell me nothing since I can't hear... wait, Blind cannot speak either? Let me recheck: Blind can act but not "see a colour, gesture, or anything printed" - but Blind isn't restricted from speaking based on the table (only Deaf and Mute have speaking restrictions listed... actually Deaf can't hear/speak-related touch, Mute cannot speak, Blind's cannot column doesn't mention speech).

So Blind CAN speak. Good. This round: Mute (me) -> Blind -> Deaf. I have no info yet. I should wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows the number 8. Light is green. There are three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.

Deaf saw display=8, light=green. Looking at the manual: row 8, column green → red. So the correct wire color is red, which is wire 1.

I need to get this to Blind, but Blind already spoke this round (before me, since order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — wait, this is a new round now). Let me reconsider: the order is Mute, Blind, Deaf each round. Deaf's message just arrived at start of this new round, meaning Deaf spoke last round. Now it's my turn (Mute) in this new round, then Blind, then Deaf again.

So I speak now, and Blind will hear/see me right after. I cannot speak, only gesture, and gestures go to Deaf only (per my channels), not Blind. But wait - Blind cannot see gestures anyway ("cannot see a colour, gesture, or anything merely printed"). So gesturing to Blind would be useless even if I could send it.

I need to get "wire 1 (red)" to Blind. But I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can then speak to Blind. So I should gesture the answer to Deaf using symbols, establishing a code, and Deaf relays to Blind by speech next round.

Let me use gestures to indicate "wire 1" using numeric-ish gesture ☝ (one).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirming again: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. I saw a single gesture from Mute, looked like one raised finger, possibly indicating wire 1.

Deaf correctly interpreted my gesture as indicating wire 1. Display 8 + light green → manual says "red" → that's wire 1 (red). This matches Deaf's guess exactly.

Now Deaf needs to tell Blind to cut/use wire 1. Deaf can speak, and Blind can hear. This round Blind speaks before Deaf, so Deaf's confirmation to Blind will happen after Blind's turn this round, landing at the start of next round for Blind. Let me confirm clearly with another gesture to lock it in, since ambiguity ("possibly") remains.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 1 is red. Repeating: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue.

Good, this confirms the mapping is locked in: display 8, light green → red → wire 1. Deaf has now repeated this clearly, presumably also telling Blind directly via speech. I have nothing new to add since my gesture already confirmed wire 1 twice. I'll wait to avoid introducing confusion, letting Deaf's spoken confirmation reach Blind.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. Display shows 8, light is green. If you are asking about the first wire, it is red.

Everything is consistent and confirmed: display 8, light green → manual gives red → wire 1. Deaf has been repeating this clearly, and since Blind can hear Deaf's speech, Blind should have received this confirmation already. Nothing further needed from me.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind, I can hear you but not see your gestures. Please gesture your answers to Deaf, who will speak them to me. Manual: which wire should I cut - 1, 2, or 3? Please have Deaf relay a number.
Deaf says: Still confirming board: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue.

Blind is asking for confirmation via Deaf relay. I've already gestured "wire 1" (☝) twice to Deaf, and Deaf has confirmed understanding of wire 1 = red matches the manual lookup (display 8, green → red). I should gesture once more clearly to reinforce, since Deaf needs to relay a number to Blind and Blind hasn't received it yet in speech form.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please respond by gesturing a wire number (1, 2 or 3) to Deaf so Deaf can tell me. If cutting is unsafe right now, gesture that too, like a stop sign.
Deaf says: Instruction for Blind: cut wire 1, the red wire. Confirming board again: display 8, light green, wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Deaf has now spoken the clear instruction "cut wire 1, the red wire" - this is speech, so Blind should hear it directly (since Blind can hear). This should reach Blind at the start of next round. I don't need to do anything further since my gesture already conveyed wire 1 and Deaf has translated correctly into speech for Blind.

```
wait()
```
